messages:
ben-arch: quick follow-up to the surge-resilience RFC. need a concrete, operator-friendly play for a region that suddenly runs out of capacity while preserving data residency constraints. idea: local shadow-writes + immediate local ack (for latency), then async reconcile to canonical region. open Qs on safety and client-visible surface.

oliver-sre: shadow-writes do reduce 5xx errors but double write load. we need a clear threshold and backoff. what headroom should trigger shadow mode? :thinking: 

ben-arch: proposal: allow up to 2x short bursts (<=5m) before tiered routing; if sustained >5m, start staged redirect. keep default short to prevent long-term divergence.

anya-ml: cache coherence concerns: local reads may be stale after shadow mode. recommend we version writes (monotonic write ids) and expose a small stale window in responses so clients can decide. also tag model responses with a degraded-quality flag when using shadowed data.

sara-eng: API change required: add `X-Redwood-Residency: strict|relaxed` header so customers can opt into relaxed semantics during surge. server will emit `Rescue-Mode: shadow` when in effect. need clear docs and examples.

ben-arch: agreed. header draft: `X-Redwood-Residency: strict|relaxed`. server hints: `Rescue-Mode: shadow`, `Relay-Region: eu-west-1` when redirecting.

oliver-sre: operational safety: short lease transfer protocol to avoid split writes. flow: 1) acquire temp regional lease 2) allow shadow-writes locally 3) reconcile and swap canonical lease back when safe. avoid blocking reads.

anya-ml: for model-backed outputs, staleness can cause measurable quality drops. suggest `x-output-confidence` and telemetry to Optimize so we can alert customers of regressions. also include sample eval prompt sets in the sim.

ben-arch: policy snippet for RFC follow-up (example):
```
route_policy:
  - name: local_prefer_shadow
    priority: [local, nearby, fallback]
    residency_enforce: true
    fallback_mode: shadow_write
    max_grace_ms: 300000
```

sara-eng: can `fallback_mode` be tenant-configurable? enterprise customers might require failover=false. also need a UI flag in Console to toggle per-tenant emergency behavior.

oliver-sre: yes per-tenant flags + global circuit breaker. metrics to track: `shadow_write_rate`, `shadow_write_failures`, `migration_lag_ms`, `lease_swap_rate`, `stale_read_rate`. alert thresholds need to be explicit.

tomas: rollout plan: 1) staged sim (50% synthetic surge) 2) canary 5% traffic with real users 3) monitor SLOs & quality signals 4) progressive 25/50/100. define abort conditions (e.g., shadow_write_failures > 1% over 5m, migration_lag_ms > 5s p95).

deploy-bot: simulation queued #409 (config: 2x RPS peak, 5m sustain). results -> https://ci.internal/sim/409

anya-ml: ensure sim includes KV cache churn and model tail-latency variance. otherwise we miss emergent failure modes. add synthetic mixed-read/write patterns.

ben-arch: will update sim config. also drafting a concise operator runbook: quick rollback via forcing `X-Redwood-Residency: strict` at edge and an emergency kill-switch in LB to disable shadow mode cluster-wide. need runbook steps and exact CLI commands.

sara-eng: I'll draft customer-facing template explaining "temporary relaxed residency" and how it affects guarantees. keep language explicit: "local writes may be reconciled to your canonical region asynchronously".

ben-arch: next steps: I'll open RFC follow-up PR with policy spec, header doc, metrics list, runbook skeleton, and staged rollout plan. tagging @sara-eng for API wording and @oliver-sre for metrics thresholds.

oliver-sre: one more ops note: log enrichment for shadow writes: include `trace_id`, `origin_region`, `canonical_region`, `write_id`. that will make postmortems far easier.

ben-arch: good call. adding to PR. thanks everyone, will post link once PR is up. :thumbsup:
